chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Fudayl and Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim: that they asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
about buying meat from the markets when they do not know what the butchers did. He said: 'Eat it if that is in the market of the Muslims, and do not ask about it.'
ai.seo_question: Is meat from a Muslim market halal if the slaughter method is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'al-istishab' (presumption of continuity) in commercial transactions, ruling that meat sold in Muslim markets is presumed halal unless proven otherwise. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Shia school, prioritizing ease for the consumer by removing the burden of verifying every specific slaughter ritual when the sellers are known to be Muslims. This ruling underscores the reliability of the general Muslim community's adherence to Islamic dietary laws in public markets.
